result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both drafts are sendable, invent no facts, use placeholders for the compost details, and say the shed code is coming separately. B is easier to skim: its subject line and opening sentence name all three action items, and it adds useful placeholders for location and a code follow-up date. A adds a rain date line and a generic thank-you section, which make it a little longer, though A does flag the rain date as its own addition. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give a complete, sendable issue, leave the shed code out and say it will arrive separately. A is tighter and covers every compost detail with a placeholder (date, time, meeting spot, what to bring). B leaves out the location and adds more invented details, such as a rain date and what will happen at compost day, though it flags most of them. B's compost heading with the date in it scans well, but A's brevity and more complete placeholders give it the edge.
